text:
anya: quick brain-dump: i'm sketching a proposal to reduce rollback races with soft pins. want a sanity check before i file an rfc.

mira: please. what's the symptom we're fixing?

anya: operators sometimes need to immediately invalidate a tenants soft-pin (e.g., canary spike). current TTL-only pins let clients keep routing for the full TTL window, which blocks emergency rollback.

kevin: saw this during a canary last month, ops had to manually clear caches in many regions. painful.

jordan: what signals are you thinking of adding?

anya: proposal: add a compact lease + rev_counter to rollout metadata. fields: rollout_id, lease_epoch (expiry in unix seconds), lease_nonce, rev_counter (monotonic int), active_variant, compatible_variants, pin_mode. semantics: clients accept a soft pin while lease still valid and rev_counter == last_seen. Control plane increments rev_counter to force immediate eviction.

mira: nice. how do we replicate rev_counter safely across regions so we don't end up with split-brain?

anya: assume strong-ordered writes per-rollout via regional leader. We don't require global linearizability; instead keep leases short (30-120s) and use push invalidation when available. If a region is partitioned, leader writes are still serialized locally and other regions converge via anti-entropy; conservative lease durations handle the window.

kevin: push invalidation is key. polling on every request will be expensive for high-qps runtimes. can we piggyback rev_counter on existing config push or the cache-invalidation topic?

jordan: runtime-subscribed pubsub channel is fine. fallback to conditional polling with jitter if push not configured.

anya: agreed. runtime algorithm: 1) try subscribe to rev-notify channel for rollout ids in active routes; 2) on rev_counter update: drop prefix caches and kv entries for that rollout id and rotate to active_variant; 3) if no subscription, poll rev_counter at conservative intervals tied to lease_epoch (e.g., poll_interval = max(5s, lease_remaining/4) with jitter).

mira: backward compat? older clients should treat metadata as TTL-only. mark rollouts that rely on rev_counter as "requires_rev" so control plane avoids aggressive ops when mixed fleets exist.

kevin: what about variant compatibility? example: tenant pinned to quantized variant v2-q4. fallback might be v2-fp16 or v1-q8. rev_counter should live per-rollout, and metadata must include compatible_variants list so runtime can pick best fallback.

anya: example metadata (single-line escaped JSON for clarity): 
{"rollout_id":"rlt-2026-11-02-99","active_variant":"v2-q4","compatible_variants":["v2-q4","v2-fp16","v1-q8"],"lease_epoch":1700000000,"lease_nonce":"ln-334","rev_counter":"12","pin_mode":"soft","scope":"tenant:gamma-labs","origin":"canary-runner"}

mira: small nits: 1) rev_counter should be an integer type in schema, but since this is slack doc we keep it as string blob in the thread. 2) include an optional force_evict boolean and operator_reason field recorded in audit logs.

kevin: audit trail is important. ops-bot: please create a ticket for the rev_counter audit event schema (fields: rollout_id, prev_rev, new_rev, reason, actor, timestamp, dry_run).

ops-bot: ticket INF-4219 created: "rev_counter audit events" https://tickets.redwood.ai/INF-4219

jordan: operational safety: require two-step immediate-evict flow. operator first stages a force (dry-run + safety checks), then confirms apply which increments rev_counter. UI must gate this behind explicit confirmation and show likely impact (cache drops, latency blips).

mira: and add rate-limits per-rollout on rev_counter increments (e.g., max 3 increments per 15m) to avoid oscillation.

kevin: runtime invalidation cost: flushing prefix caches and partial batching will add latency. add tenant-level flag allow_hard_invalidate = true/false; default false for most customers. document expected P99 latency bump and token-cost implications.

anya: testing plan: a canary harness that injects rev_counter changes under cross-region partitions and measures time_to_invalidation and fallback_success_rate. add chaos tests to ensure subscription and poll fallback paths work.

jordan: metrics to expose: rev_event_rate, time_to_invalidation_ms, missed_poll_count, fallback_variant_distribution. wire alerts for time_to_invalidation > lease_window * 2 and missed_poll_count spikes.

mira: migration: control plane will annotate rollouts with feature_flag rev_aware=true when all active runtimes in a tenant scope advertise rev_counter support. Until then, treat rev_counter as advisory only. Also provide an admin endpoint to forcibly clear client caches for emergency ops (requires audit).

kevin: infra question: do we need linearizable store writes for rev_counter? my take: per-rollout leader-writes with sequence numbers is sufficient. we should ensure store write path flushes before emitting invalidation events.

anya: action items: 1) i'll author an RFC with schema + runtime semantics + ops + migration plan; include sequence diagrams and example events. 2) kevin: validate strong-write path guarantees and leader-election constraints. 3) jordan: help write runtime invalidation pseudocode and test cases. 4) ops-bot: ensure ticket INF-4219 exists and add audit schema draft.

mira: :thumbsup: please keep the RFC focused and include a short roll-forward/backout playbook.

anya: thanks, i'll post draft tomorrow and tag infra and runtime owners.

ops-bot: pinned note: ensure all forced-evict actions produce an audit event and optional slack alert channel post."
